text: Rain moved across the courtyard. By the door, a pair of boots waited beneath a coat that had almost dried.
The last bus turned the corner. Its lights slipped between the houses, and the street settled into quiet.
A cup stood beside the open notebook. The tea had cooled before she found the words she wanted.
He lifted the latch and let the gate swing shut behind him. The garden smelled of wet earth.
Morning arrived slowly in the kitchen. A thin line of sunlight crossed the table and reached the empty chair.
The shopkeeper folded the paper bag twice. Outside, the first few drops darkened the pavement.
At the edge of the field, the fence leaned into the grass. Nothing moved except a loose strand of wire.
She left the window open a little. From the harbour came the low sound of an engine starting.
